title: C197D — Starter Motor Connector
introduction:
I read this reference like an address label for a connection: identify the connector first, then match the drawing’s cavity label to the pin-assignment table. The identification table describes the connector, the table beneath the drawing links it to a harness, and the final table maps the cavity to its circuit and recorded wire details.

The drawing shows a circular body, a central labeled cavity, a rectangular extension on the left and a projecting tab at the upper right. Those features help you navigate the illustration; they do not establish which way to view the physical connector. This is an identification and circuit-reading guide. Access, electrical testing and replacement need their matching procedures. The gauge convention and the meanings of the Size and Used codes are not defined here, so I leave those entries uninterpreted.

edits.why: I match the cavity label in the center of the drawing to the Cavity column below. The nearby Fpn, Size and Harness Id table supplies the associated identification data; it does not establish a viewing direction or a replacement procedure.

Read across the cavity’s row to connect its Circuit Number with the recorded Color, Gauge, Function and Terminal Part Number. Keep the function wording as an identifying label rather than treating it as a test instruction. A blank Qualifier supplies no additional applicability information.
